france24fr.title: Séismes au Venezuela : vers une crise humanitaire ?
france24fr.description: Les Etats-Unis ont poursuivi leur mobilisation lundi au Venezuela pour muscler une aide internationale "vitale", cinq jours après le double séisme qui a fait au moins 1.719 morts.

france24fr.title: En Afrique du Sud, journée à risque en pleine campagne contre les immigrés
france24fr.description: En ce 30 juin, date d'un ultimatum fixé en dehors de tout cadre légal par des groupes citoyens très structurés pour intimer aux étrangers sans papiers l'ordre de quitter le pays, la police est déployée en masse en Afrique du Sud pour parer à d'éventuelles violences.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les Ivoiriens peuvent-ils faire vaciller les redoutables Norvégiens ?
france24fr.description: Pour la première fois de son histoire, la Côte d'Ivoire s'est qualifiée pour la phase à élimination directe d'un Mondial. Pour poursuivre encore plus loin leur aventure, les Ivoiriens vont devoir vaincre la Norvège et sa machine à buts Erling Haaland.

france24fr.title: Une explosion volontaire fait trois blessés à Monaco, dont un oligarque ukrainien
france24fr.description: Un suspect a déposé, lundi, un sac dans le hall d'un immeuble résidentiel à Monaco, provoquant une explosion, avant de fuir, rapportent les autorités. Au moins trois personnes ont été blessées, dont l'oligarque ukrainien Vadim Ermolaev, selon une source proche du dossier. Le suspect est toujours recherché.

france24fr.title: Comment fonctionnera la nouvelle taxe européenne sur les petits colis importés de l'étranger ?
france24fr.description: À compter de mercredi, les petits colis importés dans l'UE, jusqu'ici exemptés de droits de douane, seront soumis à une nouvelle taxe européenne. Une taxe temporaire mise en place jusqu'à une refonte en profondeur du système douanier européen, prévue dans deux ans.

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde : le Paraguay élimine l'Allemagne dès les 16es de finale
france24fr.description: Le Paraguay a créé la sensation en battant l’Allemagne en 16es de finale de la Coupe du monde (1-1, 4 tab à 3). Le Paraguay pourrait affronter la France au tour suivant.

france24fr.title: Washington ou "Trumptown" : la tentation du culte de la personnalité architectural
france24fr.description: Rénovation d’un golf municipal, extensions à la Maison Blanche, rêves d’arc de triomphe : Donald Trump semble avoir 1 001 projets pour Washington. Pourquoi le président puise-t-il ainsi dans son expérience de magnat de l’immobilier pour laisser sa marque sur la capitale américaine ? Une tentation qui existe par ailleurs chez la plupart des dirigeants ayant des tendances autocratiques.

france24fr.title: Ultimatum anti-immigrés en Afrique du Sud : "Une nation sur le fil du rasoir"
france24fr.description: A la Une de la presse, ce mardi 30 juin, l’expiration, aujourd’hui, en Afrique du Sud, de l’ultimatum exigeant le départ des migrants sans-papiers. Les réactions à la décision de la Cour suprême américaine de mettre fin à l’indépendance des agences fédérales, sauf à celle de la Fed. Le combat d’une enseignante mexicaine pour tenter d’arracher ses élèves au fléau du narcotrafic. Et le retour en pleine lumière du capitaine des Bleus, Kylian Mbappé.

france24fr.title: "Mbappé, on arrive !" : l’euphorie des supporters après l’exploit du Paraguay
france24fr.description: C’est le premier exploit des 16es de finale du Mondial : le Paraguay a créé la sensation lundi à Boston en éliminant l’Allemagne aux tirs au but. À la sortie du stade, France 24 a recueilli les réactions des supporters paraguayens, entre euphorie, surprise et fierté, après cette victoire historique.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : résultats, articles et temps forts de la nuit
france24fr.description: Le Brésil qui bataille contre le Japon, l'Allemagne sortie par le Paraguay et le Maroc vainqueur des Pays-Bas à l'arraché. Retrouvez les résultats des matches disputés dans la nuit, les temps forts et les derniers articles de France 24 sur la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.description: Le Maroc a remporté le choc des 16es de finale contre les Pays-Bas à Monterrey. Menés après un but de Cody Gakpo, les Lions de l'Atlas ont trouvé les ressources pour égaliser. Avant de s'imposer lors de la séance de tirs au but (1-1, t.a.b. 3-2) grâce à un immense Yassine Bono.

france24fr.title: Après les séismes au Venezuela, le port de La Guaira est à nouveau opérationnel
france24fr.description: L'armée américaine, qui a déployé 130 Marines après le double séisme, a annoncé lundi que le port de la ville de La Guaira était à nouveau opérationnel, permettant le débarquement d'aide humanitaire. La catastrophe a fait au moins 1 719 morts.

france24fr.title: Téhéran rejette toute ingérence dans le contrôle et le déminage du détroit d'Ormuz
france24fr.description: Le président français et le sultan d'Oman ont plaidé lundi pour une "navigation libre, sans conditions ni restrictions" dans le détroit d'Ormuz et convenu d'y mener des "opérations de déminage conjointes". Pour les responsables iraniens, il n'est pas question que d'autres pays interviennent pour le déminage ou le contrôle du détroit d'Ormuz. En négociations avec Oman, Téhéran "veut garder le contrôle" de cette zone stratégique, rappelle Siavosh Ghazi, correspondant pour France 24 à Téhéran.

france24fr.title: Un projet de loi sur l'enfance examiné à l'Assemblée, bientôt élargi après l'affaire Lyhanna
france24fr.description: Un projet de loi sur la protection des enfants est examiné à partir de mardi par une commission spéciale à l'Assemblée, avant d'être enrichi de mesures promises par le gouvernement après le meurtre de la collégienne Lyhanna.

france24fr.title: Explosion à Monaco : la traque du suspect est lancée dans la principauté et en France
france24fr.description: Une explosion a retenti, lundi soir, à Monaco, faisant trois blessés - dont un oligarque ukrainien. "Ce qui est désormais crucial, c'est la traque du suspect, de l'individu qui a laissé le sac avant de fuir", rapporte Aude Kersulec, journaliste de France 24 à Monaco. Vraisemblablement, il devrait se trouver en France, d'où une "collaboration renforcée" entre les deux pays pour le retrouver.

france24fr.title: En direct : des délégations américaines et iraniennes au Qatar, pas de réunion bilatérale confirmée
france24fr.description: L'Iran a annoncé l'envoi d'une délégation au Qatar mardi pour des rencontres techniques sans négociations directes avec le camp adverse. De son côté, Washington a fait savoir que les émissaires Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner se rendraient sur place "cette semaine pour participer à des réunions de haut niveau". Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.description: Des groupes de citoyens ont lancé en Afrique du Sud un ultimatum exigeant que les étrangers sans papiers quittent le territoire avant le 30 juin, une initiative non validée par le gouvernement. Le National Joint Operational and Intelligence Structure estime, lundi, que "plus de 25 000 ressortissants étrangers ont été rapatriés" pour leur sécurité.

spiegel.title: WhatsApp: So funktioniert die Kommunikation über Benutzernamen
spiegel.description: Nutzername statt Telefonnummer: Was andere Messenger längst bieten, ist bald auch bei WhatsApp möglich. Das neue Feature soll die Privatsphäre schützen.

spiegel.title: Arbeitsmarkt: Zahl der Arbeitslosen sinkt im Juni leicht
spiegel.description: Am Ende des ersten Halbjahres sind in Deutschland weniger als drei Millionen Menschen arbeitslos – aber mehr als im vergangenen Jahr. Die anhaltend schwache Konjunktur verhindert mehr Beschäftigung.

spiegel.title: Angelina Jolie: Seit zehn Jahren kein Date, jetzt will sie »wieder frei sein«
spiegel.description: Angelina Jolie ließ sich 2016 von Brad Pitt scheiden, seitdem will sie kein ernsthaftes Date gehabt haben. Nun wünschen sich ihre Töchter etwas anderes für sie: »Ich muss wieder leben.«

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Deutschland scheitert – das Foxborough-Fiasko
spiegel.description: Der deutsche WM-Traum ist mit einer Blamage im Sechzehntelfinale geplatzt. Für DFB-Kapitän Kimmich ist es bereits das dritte WM-Scheitern. In seiner Enttäuschung zeigt er jedoch Größe – anders als der Bundestrainer.

spiegel.title: Passagiermaschine offenbar beim Anflug auf New Yorker Flughafen von Drohne getroffen
spiegel.description: Ein Pilot meldet, dass sein Airbus auf dem Weg zum Flughafen JFK von einer Drohne getroffen wurde. Wenig später gibt es offenbar einen Beinaheunfall zwischen einem Helikopter und einem ferngesteuerten Flugzeug.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Jonathan Tahs Tor wird aberkannt - die Fehler des Schiedsrichters
spiegel.description: Das WM-Aus des DFB-Teams beschäftigt Fußball-Deutschland. Wegen der schwachen Leistung, aber auch wegen eines Fehlers des Schiedsrichters. Das Tor von Jonathan Tah hätte nicht zurückgenommen werden dürfen.

spiegel.title: Kündigung: Anwältin erklärt, wie Beschäftigte sich gegen Druck wehren können
spiegel.description: Mira Ney berät Menschen, die gerade ihre Privilegien oder ihre Jobs verlieren. Die Arbeitsrechtlerin weiß, wann Arbeitgeber zu weit gehen und wie Beschäftigte sich wehren können.

spiegel.title: Northvolt: Reiche will Projektgesellschaft rasch an US-Start-up verkaufen
spiegel.description: Weitgehend unbemerkt hat Wirtschaftsministerin Reiche die deutsche Northvolt-Projektgesellschaft verstaatlichen lassen. Nun sollen die Reste schnell an ein US-Start-up gehen. Gibt es dabei eine verdeckte Förderung?

observador.title: As notícias das 10h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: “O amor não é só química, mas sem química não haveria amor”
observador.description: “As pessoas mais emotivas não são mais frágeis”, revela Nuno Maulide em “A Química das emoções”, onde alerta para o amor que nos desarma e defende que as melhores ideias nasceram do tédio

observador.title: Livre quer compensar "vontade distorcida" dos eleitores
observador.description: Neste Explicador, a co-porta-voz do Livre Isabel Mendes Lopes desvaloriza a não recandidatura ao mesmo cargo de Rui Tavares, lembrando que a liderança do Livre é "partilhada". Ainda, eleições.

observador.title: Sócrates vai ficar rico à custa dos contribuintes?
observador.description: José Sócrates consegue 15 mil euros do Estado e Bugalho brilha a bater no PS ao atacar o tema da imigração. O canal da PSU morre e a ERC anda perdida a caçar morcegos digitais.

observador.title: Dia 20 do Mundial 2026. França e Noruega entram em campo
observador.description: A França, campeã mundial em 1998 e 2018, vai jogar contra Suécia. Já a Noruega irá enfrentar a Costa do Marfim, vencedora da Taça das Nações Africanas em 2024.

observador.title: 9h. PS acusa Governo de estigmatizar juntamente com o Chega
observador.description: Declarações de Eurico Brilhante Dias, nas jornadas parlamentares. Ainda, já chegou a Portugal o avião que traz 17 cidadãos que estavam na Venezuela: 13 são portugueses e quatro são estrangeiros.

observador.title: Vale dos Judeus. Greve dos guardas prolonga-se até agosto
observador.description: O presidente do sindicato dos guardas prisionais confirma que a greve está com adesão acima dos 90%. O sindicato exige a instalação de torres, as redes nos pátios e a reestruturação dos horários.

observador.title: Gomas, fado e Moedas: O "duro trabalho" no Rock in Rio
observador.description: Entre gomas na zona VIP e o fado de Emídio Guerreiro, o Rock in Rio foi uma festa. Carlos Moedas jura que "trabalha" enquanto vê o "avô" Rod Stewart.

observador.title: Vamos pagar a Sócrates? Depois não culpem o populismo
observador.description: O PSD (que arranjou uma solução), o Ministério das Finanças (que não nos disse nada) e a nossa Justiça (que precisa de uma mudança radical) são o Bom, o Mau e o Vilão.

observador.title: Prazo para limpar terrenos termina esta terça-feira
observador.description: O prazo para limpeza de terrenos para prevenção de incêndios acaba esta sexta-feira. Proprietários florestais pedem que não sejam aplicadas coimas de imediato a quem ainda está a trabalhar.

observador.title: Adeus Alemanha e o "teatrinho" de 6 golos da Áustria
observador.description: A Alemanha caiu nos penáltis e Bielsa foi à vida. Entre um jogo perigoso do Brasil com o Japão, surge o escândalo: um 3-3 da Áustria-Argélia que cheira a jogo combinado.

observador.title: Droga: 25 anos após descriminalização, pesadelo voltou?
observador.description: O regresso a um passado que se imaginava ultrapassado: toxicodependentes consumem a céu aberto no centro de cidades como Lisboa e Porto. Residentes queixam-se da insegurança e do convívio com droga.

observador.title: Acesso precoce a redes sociais é prejudicial às crianças
observador.description: No Dia Mundial das Redes Sociais, professores e psicólogos alertam: o acesso precoce deixa marcas no desenvolvimento cognitivo e socioemocional difíceis de reverter.

observador.title: Caos, emoção e uma aliança (no dedo) Portugal-Áustria
observador.description: Nesta newsletter tem todas as informações de que precisa para começar o dia, da política à cultura, passando pelo Mundial de Futebol, com direito surpresas.

observador.title: 8h. Voo com portugueses retirados da Venezuela chegou hoje
observador.description: Aterrou no Aeródromo Militar de Figo Maduro e trouxe 17 cidadãos a bordo. Ainda, calor nos próximos dias vai aumentar o risco de incêndio em todo o país.

observador.title: Milei apoia Flávio Bolsonaro nas presidenciais
observador.description: Presidente argentino e senador brasileiro encontraram-se à margem de um evento da Israel Allies Foundation. Flávio Bolsonaro é apontado como principal rival de Lula, mas perdeu terreno nas sondagens.

observador.title: "A Ucrânia tem capacidade para impor uma derrota à Rússia"
observador.description: Miguel Baumgartner destaca que a Ucrânia pode forçar uma derrota política à Rússia e negociar em igualdade. Ainda acrescenta que o Irão controla o tempo negocial perante uns EUA sob pressão eleitoral.

observador.title: Venezuela. Corina Machado impedida de entrar no país
observador.description: María Corina Machado denuncia que Delcy Rodríguez impediu a sua entrada no país encerrando o espaço aéreo. A notícia é do El Nacional. Ainda, Bruxelas dá dois meses a Portugal para legislar a PSU.

elpais.title: La familia que volvió desde España a Venezuela y quedó sepultada por los terremotos
elpais.description: Un amigo telefonea desde Galicia para mover lo inamovible. Al otro lado del océano, en Venezuela, una mujer lleva seis días sin separarse del edificio donde están sepultados sus padres, su hermano y sus dos sobrinos

elpais.title: La Complutense sanciona a Monedero a un año de suspensión de funciones por acoso sexista
elpais.description: El fundador de Podemos recibió una denuncia del entorno académico hace un año, después de que salieran otras acusaciones dentro del partido

elpais.title: El fiscal sitúa al exministro Fernández Díaz al frente de la Operación Kitchen: “Se ha acreditado su participación”
elpais.description: El juicio afronta su recta final con las conclusiones de acusaciones y defensas

elpais.title: Finlandia sale a la caza de maestras españolas de Infantil: “Les ofrecemos 3.200 euros brutos al mes y casa garantizada”
elpais.description: El país nórdico no genera bastantes profesores para cubrir los que necesita por clase, según la ley: “A ratos somos 5 docentes para 14 alumnos”

elpais.title: La pareja de Isak Andic ya ha cobrado los 27 millones pactados con los hijos del fundador de Mango
elpais.description: Estefanía Knuth declara este martes, como testigo, ante la jueza que investiga a Jonathan Andic por el homicidio de su padre

elpais.title: Paraguay elimina a la apagada Alemania en los penaltis para firmar la primera gran hazaña en las eliminatorias del Mundial
elpais.description: El equipo de Alfaro, que se adelantó con un gol de Enciso antes de que empatara Havertz, sella un ejercicio de resistencia ante una Mannschaft sin ideas y se medirá en octavos con el ganador del Francia - Suecia

elpais.title: Marruecos elimina a Países Bajos en los penaltis con un Bono providencial
elpais.description: La selección africana remonta el gol de Gakpo y elimina a una Oranje que nunca logró imponer su juego

elpais.title: Brasil remonta a la japonesa con un gran Casemiro y un gol de Martinelli en el último suspiro
elpais.description: La Canarinha se sobrepone al tanto de Japón liderada por el veterano mediocentro, autor del empate, y el empeño driblador de Vinicius en un segundo tiempo de acoso y derribo culminado por el extremo del Arsenal en el descuento

elpais.title: Lamine Yamal busca su pareja en la banda derecha
elpais.description: De la Fuente ha alternado a Pedro Porro y a Llorente como compañeros del 19

elpais.title: El irresistible ascenso de la emperatriz de Chamberí
elpais.description: El periodista David Fernández narra a partir de datos, confidencias e intrigas la berlanguiana historia de la llegada al poder de Isabel Díaz Ayuso y los últimos años de la derecha madrileña

elpais.title: La invasión de los ladrones de mentes
elpais.description: Ni el antisanchismo ambiental más intenso justifica las soluciones penales extraordinarias. Ya hemos visto a dónde nos llevó la resolución penal del conflicto catalán

elpais.title: El silencio de las secretarias
elpais.description: Los curritos tardamos demasiado en comprender que nuestros exiguos salarios dependen mucho más de los discretos silencios que de las ideas brillantes.

elpais.title: En la biblioteca de Martín Caparrós: “Tras la ELA, proyecto mis libros en la pared y me siento el rey del mundo”
elpais.description: El escritor ha reinventado su forma de leer en casa eliminando los libros físicos para manejar toda su biblioteca con un dedo

elpais.title: Feijóo insinúa que la ‘ley de nietos’ permite manipular el censo tras haber defendido su nacionalización masiva
elpais.description: El PP se une a las denuncias de Vox de que conceder el pasaporte a los descendientes de españoles persigue la “ingeniería electoral”

elpais.title: Indignación entre los diplomáticos por las insinuaciones de PP y Vox sobre su complicidad en un supuesto fraude electoral
elpais.description: Alberto Virella, presidente de la asociación mayoritaria de la carrera, defiende la profesionalidad y honorabilidad del personal consular

elpais.title: Sánchez: “Sin inmigración, España perdería un 19% de su PIB en 2050″
elpais.description: El Gobierno presenta un plan de integración con un presupuesto de 500 millones de euros

elpais.title: Maíllo, a Moreno: “Ya se le acabó el moderado. Va a tener que asumir la agenda de Abascal”
elpais.description: El dirigente popular responde a los grupos de la oposición con el no de Vox a su investidura

elpais.title: La Audiencia Nacional actúa ahora contra quienes ayudaron a la presunta trama de Leire Díez a influir en operaciones de la SEPI
elpais.description: El juez Santiago Pedraz impulsa esta línea de investigación con la imputación de otras 25 personas, entre empresarios y responsables públicos

republika.title: Bari, omicidio in pieno giorno: ucciso un operaio in bici a pochi metri dalla piazza di Carbonara
republika.description: Agguato in via De Marinis. L’uomo è stato colpito alla testa mentre era in bici: si segue la pista passionale

republika.title: Appello di Leone XIV ai Lefebvriani: “Tornate sui vostri passi, scisma di estrema gravità”
republika.description: Domani in Svizzera in programma le ordinazioni episcopali che farebbero scattare scomunica e scisma. “Prego per voi, perché lacerare la Tunica inconsutile di Cristo è un peccato di estrema gravità”

republika.title: Vannacci a Meloni: “Tiri fuori gli attributi, sì a preferenze vere nella legge elettorale”
republika.description: L’ex generale risponde alla parole della premier: “La premier chiede fiducia a scatola chiusa, le alleanze si fanno in due”

republika.title: Orlando Gill, chi è il portiere pararigori del Paraguay che ha eliminato la Germania
republika.description: Si è venduto quasi tutto per pagare le cure del figlio che appena nato rischiava di morire, dopo il flop contro gli Usa è stato criticato ferocemente da Chilavert. Oggi è l’eroe dell’Albirroja qualificata agli ottavi del Mondiale

republika.title: Effetto Ancelotti, la calma di Carletto per tranquillizzare il Brasile
republika.description: La rimonta contro il Giappone nata più che dai cambi da come il ct italiano ha saputo mantenere tranquilla la squadra. Il premio per la qualificazione agli ottavi è un giorno e mezzo di riposo

republika.title: Sigfrido Ranucci: “La giustizia non mi ha lasciato solo. Dalla Rai non mi aspetto più nulla”
republika.description: Dopo l'arresto di quattro persone che hanno materialmente eseguito l’attenato, parla il conduttore: “Il pm Carlo Villani mi aveva promesso che li avrebbe presi e l’ha fatto. Ma l’indagine non è ancora finita”

republika.title: Sondaggi politici: Vannacci cresce ancora e supera la Lega, male FdI
republika.description: La rilevazione settimanale di Swg per il Tg La7 sulle intenzioni di voto degli italiani

republika.title: Il record del caccia russo: abbatte un jet ucraino a 190 chilometri di distanza
republika.description: Mosca utilizza missili a lunghissimo raggio per colpire senza correre rischi. E’ la nuova dimensione della guerra aerea, combattuta a distanze anche di 300 chilometri

republika.title: Caldo estremo in 25 città bollino rosso. In arrivo temporali
republika.description: In Europa 35 gradi per almeno 130 milioni di persone

republika.title: Olanda già fuori, il Marocco vince ai rigori e vola agli ottavi dei Mondiali
republika.description: Diop nel recupero risponde alla rete di Gakpo, dal dischetto decisivo Saibari dopo l’errore di Summerville. Gli africani sfideranno il Canada

republika.title: Attentato dinamitardo contro Sigfrido Ranucci, 4 arresti. “Hanno agito in cambio di denaro”
republika.description: L’accusa è detenzione di esplosivi e danneggiamento con l'aggravante del metodo mafioso

republika.title: Delusione Germania, eliminata ai sedicesimi: il Paraguay vince ai rigori
republika.description: Tempi regolamentari e supplementari finiti 1-1 per le reti di Enciso e Havertz. Dal dischetto si va a oltranza, decisivo l’errore di Tah. Canale non sbaglia nel momento della verità

republika.title: Chi è l’oligarca ucraino colpito nell’attentato del Principato di Monaco
republika.description: Si tratterebbe di Vadim Ermolaev, 58 anni: patrimonio enorme, finito sotto inchiesta a Kiev

republika.title: Meloni: “Infrangere il tabù della destra al Quirinale”. Vannacci? “Sta all’opposizione”
republika.description:
La presidente del Consiglio torna in tv ospite di Porro su Rete 4. E per la prima volta allude in maniera esplicita alla scalata al Colle. Prende le distanze
ma non chiude con Fn. E su Trump: “Né antiamericana, né inginocchiata”

republika.title: Mollicone: “Dialogo con il generale solo se smette di votarci contro”
republika.description: Il presidente FdI della commissione Cultura della Camera: “Il capo di Fn deve fare chiarezza. Finora non ha mai preso le distanze da Putin sull’Ucraina”

republika.title: Cruciani: “Mi piacciono i mostri. Voglio discutere di idee estreme”
republika.description: Il giornalista domenica ha intervistato Salvini e poi Vannacci: “Il generale unisce carisma militare e resistenza da maratoneta. Lui è il nuovo, io l’ho già votato”

republika.title: “Primarie per le città”. Ma gli alleati bocciano la proposta di Salvini
republika.description: Tajani chiude la porta: “Lasciamo perdere le chiacchiere, i vertici decidono i nomi migliori”

nyt.title: Trump Renews Threat to Fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook After Supreme Court Ruling
nyt.description: President Trump promised to “take appropriate action immediately” against Lisa Cook, the Fed governor he had tried to fire, even as the court affirmed that Fed officials can be fired only for cause.

nyt.title: Supreme Court Expands Trump’s Power to Fire Officials but Prevents Lisa Cook Removal
nyt.description: In twin rulings, the Supreme Court affirmed the Fed’s independence and said its leaders could not be fired at will, but said President Trump could fire other independent regulators for any reason.

nyt.title: Supreme Court Decision on Late-Arriving Mail-In Ballots Grants Relief to 18 States
nyt.description: The Supreme Court ruled on Monday that state laws allowing ballots to arrive after Election Day are legal. The decision is the latest in a series of setbacks for President Trump’s efforts to regulate elections.

nyt.title: Supreme Court Rejects Trump’s Request to Appeal $5 Million Verdict in E. Jean Carroll Case
nyt.description: President Trump had asked the justices to intervene after a jury found that he had sexually abused and defamed the writer E. Jean Carroll.

nyt.title: ‘No One’s Coming to Save Us but Us’: Gen Z Runs for Office
nyt.description: Melat Kiros’s challenge Tuesday to Representative Diana DeGette, who was elected the year before Ms. Kiros was born, is the latest Gen Z test in a year defined by generational upheaval.

nyt.title: California Hopes to Speed Up Election Results With $40 Million Infusion
nyt.description: It took six days to determine the outcome of the primary for Los Angeles mayor, and seven for the governor’s race.

nyt.title: Kean Set to Speak at the Capitol After Mysterious Absence
nyt.description: After months of silence, Representative Tom Kean Jr. was expected to deliver a speech explaining his 116-day absence from Congress.

nyt.title: Two Dan Sullivans to Appear on Alaska Senate Ballot, State High Court Rules
nyt.description: Republicans had sought the removal of a little-known candidate with the same name as the incumbent senator, arguing that he was not a “good faith” candidate.

nyt.title: Judge Orders Trump to End Efforts to Kill Hudson Tunnel Funding
nyt.description: A federal judge says that the administration’s attempts to block money for the $16 billion rail project were “flagrantly” illegal.

nyt.title: Trump on Legislation to Address the Nation’s Housing Crisis: ‘It’s a Yawn’
nyt.description: Time and again, President Trump has brushed off Americans’ concerns about the economy and their financial situations.

nyt.title: Clash Unfolds as Trump Administration Pushes Intelligence Agencies to Share Foreign Espionage Targets
nyt.description: The clash reflects increasing skepticism of the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, which has been willing to pursue President Trump’s priorities.

nyt.title: Moscow Is Attacked by Dozens of Drones, Its Mayor Says
nyt.description: Sergei Sobyanin said the Russian military had shot down more than 60 drones. He did not report any injuries.

nyt.title: In San Francisco’s A.I. Era, Even $180,000 Tech Salaries Are No Longer Enough
nyt.description: As OpenAI and Anthropic prepare to go public, tech workers making six figures are grousing that they cannot compete with the new A.I. elite. Some doubt they can afford to stay.

nyt.title: A.I. ‘Employees’ Might Disrupt Work in Unexpected Ways
nyt.description: Scholars say the “unknown unknowns” of using artificial intelligence in the workplace may be undermining the technology’s advertised benefits.

nyt.title: $22,000 Per Hour: Assistants Use a Legislative Loophole to Outearn Surgeons
nyt.description: A law meant to end surprise medical billing has led to large paydays for some surgical assistants, who can earn far more than the doctors they help.

nyt.title: Former Chinese Billionaire and Bannon Associate Is Sentenced for Fraud
nyt.description: The businessman courted U.S. conservatives as an anti-Communist crusader while using his supporters’ money to buy lavish homes and a Bugatti supercar.

nyt.title: See Day-by-Day Forecast as Heat Wave Engulfs U.S. Ahead of the July 4 Weekend
nyt.description: Dangerous heat is expected across much of the country through the Fourth of July weekend.

nyt.title: Emily Barker Loved Fighting Fires. She Died in One She Couldn’t Escape.
nyt.description: Emily Barker was one of two women who died fighting a large forest fire in Colorado this week.

npr.title: Venezuelans deported from the U.S. were killed hours later in powerful quakes
npr.description: 146 Venezuelans were deported from Texas to Caracas on June 24. Hours later, while the deportees were in a guarded hotel, powerful twin earthquakes struck.

npr.title: Iran war supercharges pivot to renewable energy
npr.description: The Iran war and high oil and gas prices have supercharged the adoption of renewables and EVs across the world. Some experts wonder if this year could be the peak of oil demand.

npr.title: Explosion in Monaco injures 3, including Ukrainian tycoon
npr.description: A blast from an explosive device has seriously injured three people at a residential building in Monaco, and the attacker fled to France, local authorities said.

npr.title: Chinese billionaire Guo Wengui gets 30 years in U.S. prison for fraud conviction
npr.description: Guo said he came to the U.S. to destroy the Chinese Communist Party. But the judge said he instead diverted investor money to live lavishly.

npr.title: Venezuela's deadly quakes put its U.S.-backed government to the test
npr.description: Venezuela's La Guaira state bore the brunt of the earthquake damage, bringing memories of a 1999 disaster that became President Hugo Chávez's first major test. Now, it's the acting leader's challenge.

npr.title: Pakistani airstrikes kill 36 civilians in Afghanistan and wound 160, officials say
npr.description: Pakistan says it targeted militant hideouts along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in response to militant attacks across Pakistan. Afghanistan condemned the strikes as acts of aggression.

npr.title: U.S. and Iran exchange fire despite ceasefire. And, Trump nominates a new head of ICE
npr.description: The U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes over the weekend, putting their latest ceasefire in jeopardy. And, Trump has nominated a former Oklahoma state trooper to head Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

npr.title: Trump says the U.S. and Iran will meet in Qatar after weekend attacks
npr.description: President Trump said talks with Iran would resume Tuesday in Qatar, despite the two sides trading attacks in the Gulf over the weekend. Iran did not confirm whether it will participate.

npr.title: Former Iran nuclear deal negotiator on what U.S.-Iran 'new normal' looks like
npr.description: NPR's Leila Fadel asks former national security adviser and 2015 Iran deal negotiator Jake Sullivan about ceasefire talks amid new strikes by the U.S. and Iran.

npr.title: Could neo-Nazi youth, or 'active clubs,' have played a role in Belfast riots?
npr.description: In the wake of racist mob violence in Northern Ireland, there has been attention on "active clubs," a global network of fascist, white nationalist youth groups that center activities around mixed martial arts.

lanacion.description: Conoce qué decide la Corte Suprema sobre la ciudadanía por nacimiento en EE.UU. y cómo el fallo podría afectar a miles de familias migrantes.

lanacion.description: Fue atacado por hinchas, luego de un partido de fútbol en la localidad de Carcarañá, en Santa Fe

lanacion.description: En 2024, un frigorífico argentino fue la primera víctima conocida de una red de ciberfraude; un año después, se sumó una fábrica de envases plásticos de Beccar; en total fueron 40 compañías argentinas estafadas por el troyano bancario Mekotio

lanacion.description: El partido de 16avos de final se disputará este martes a las 18 (hora argentina) en el estadio de Nueva York; Paraguay espera por el ganador

lanacion.description: La idea de llevar a la pantalla una parodia no parecía una apuesta sencilla, pero la enorme química que se generó en el set echó por tierra los malos presagios para ver nacer a una verdadera obra maestra

lanacion.title: Madonna y los 40 años de True Blue: su historia de amor con Sean Penn, su incursión “latina” y la canción que generó una gran controversia

phys-org.title: How embryonic cells 'read' their boundaries to organize themselves
phys-org.description: In the earliest stages of life, mammalian embryos start as a disorganized cluster of cells. As development progresses, these cells become organized into well-defined shapes and structures. This process happens again and again during development, yet it unfolds in environments full of noise and variability. So how do individual cells know which way to point? And what determines where the embryo will form its fluid-filled cavity, a crucial step in mammalian embryonic development?

This raises a critical question: How can educators truly understand whether students are learning, rather than simply producing polished answers with AI assistance?

phys-org.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is continuing to have a disruptive impact on ever more parts of humanity. But what does it mean in the long run? A new paper, available as a preprint on arXiv from Austrian researcher Sergey Ivliev, extrapolates what the wide-scale adoption of AI means for the future of humanity in space—and in particular, what it means for the ultimate question of whether we're truly alone in the galaxy.

phys-org.description: What if the mechanical properties of a cell could be programmed like the components of a machine? Researchers at the University of Tokyo have discovered that two fundamental modes of cellular deformation—stretching and bending—can be independently controlled using different molecular building blocks. The finding provides a new strategy for engineering artificial cells, drug-delivery capsules and adaptive soft materials with precisely tailored mechanical functions.

phys-org.title: Unexpected pathway turns water and CO₂ into climate‑neutral methane on nickel–zirconia
phys-org.description: Natural gas still plays an important role in many industrial sectors, but it is a climate-damaging fossil fuel. TU Wien and the University of Innsbruck have now discovered an unexpected reaction pathway that makes it possible to synthesize natural gas, or methane (CH4), using CO2 that was previously captured from exhaust gas streams or directly from the air. In this way, methane can become climate-neutral overall.

phys-org.title: Plutonium compound unlocks rare topological quantum behavior with potential nuclear science applications
phys-org.description: Plutonium is one of the most complex elements in the periodic table. First synthesized and isolated in 1940 by scientists at the University of California, Berkeley, plutonium has been studied closely for more than eight decades. It's most often associated with its role in nuclear security, but it's also vital to nuclear power, where it is produced in reactors and can be recycled as fuel. Despite plutonium's importance, some of its most fundamental behaviors remain a mystery.

phys-org.title: New Horizons tracks solar wind slowdown as interstellar atoms add drag
phys-org.description: A new Southwest Research Institute (SwRI) study based on data from NASA's New Horizons spacecraft has uncovered insights into why the solar wind gradually slows as it moves toward the edge of the solar system and the boundary with interstellar space. The study "The Gradual Slowing of the Solar Wind in the Outer Heliosphere" is published in The Astrophysical Journal.

phys-org.title: What DC's algal bloom reveals about a growing water threat
phys-org.description: When bright green water appeared in the newly renovated Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, it drew national attention and sparked political finger-pointing. undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway

But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: Why Americans Are Wary of AI
proj-syn.description: The tech industry is asking Americans to embrace AI at a moment when trust in government is declining. While these may seem like separate issues, persuading people to trust AI will be far more difficult if they do not trust the institutions responsible for regulating it.

proj-syn.title: Why the Gulf Needs Economic Ties with Iran
proj-syn.description: Most Gulf observers agree that the old security order is dying. But none of the most commonly proposed options—buying more advanced weapons, seeking protection from new partners in the Global South, or building stronger national militaries—is sufficient on its own.

proj-syn.title: The Right Way to Tackle Developing Countries’ Cancer Crisis
proj-syn.description: Some health advocates believe that weakening intellectual-property protections and capping prices for the most advanced cancer treatments would expand access in developing countries. But this well-intentioned argument overlooks an inescapable reality: without strong incentives for innovation, such treatments would not exist.

proj-syn.title: Enforce AI Guardrails Before It’s Too Late
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration’s decision to impose export controls on Anthropic’s latest models is emblematic of the incoherent and shifting response from policymakers worldwide to the rapidly advancing AI sector. To ensure that these tools do not court disaster, governments must establish meaningful guardrails.

proj-syn.title: Is a European Single Market for Energy Such a Good Idea?
proj-syn.description: Although textbook microeconomics shows why less energy-market fragmentation would be better for Europe as a whole, that does not mean it would be a good deal for countries producing low-carbon electricity at minimal marginal cost. In fact, if more integration creates free riders, the political backlash could be profound.

proj-syn.title: China’s Failed Rebalancing
proj-syn.description: When China’s leaders first acknowledged the need to rebalance the economy nearly two decades ago, it seemed like a matter of when, not if. But with the household consumption share of Chinese GDP remaining stubbornly low, officials’ promises to boost domestic demand have lost all credibility.

proj-syn.title: Crowning a Healthy Populism
proj-syn.description: Although recent political mobilizations in Hungary, Albania, and other parts of Central and Eastern Europe could be described as populist and nationalist, they have little in common with the aggressive ethnonationalism that MAGA professes. Could they be a model for a new form of politics?

proj-syn.title: Why Rules-Based Orders Fail
proj-syn.description: For a brief period after the Cold War, Americans persuaded themselves that the liberal order had become self-sustaining. And yet, any rules-based system elaborate enough to govern and interpret its own operations will eventually confront questions that its rules cannot answer.

proj-syn.title: The Tide Is Turning Against Russia
proj-syn.description: With Ukraine reclaiming territory, mounting drone strikes deep in Russian territory, and draining Russia’s coffers, Vladimir Putin would do well to seek a negotiated freeze to the conflict. But there is no guarantee that he will, not least because he might not grasp the situation Russia is in.

proj-syn.title: Managing Sino-American Interdependence
proj-syn.description: At their summit last month, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping seemed to recognize that they are in the same boat. If either the United States or China tries to cripple or decouple from the other, it will harm its own firms, consumers, financial markets, and innovation ecosystem.

proj-syn.title: Who Gains in an AI-Supercharged Economy?
proj-syn.description: If AI delivers as promised and fundamentally transforms the economy, we will have moved from the current investment phase, where AI builders dominate, to one where AI users will reap the greatest reward. That is what happens every time an innovation becomes a general-purpose technology.

proj-syn.title: Development in a Time of Disruption
proj-syn.description: Once firms and economies ascend to market dominance, they often kick away the ladder behind them and erect barriers to market entry to stymie would-be challengers. But developing countries can and do leapfrog incumbent technologies, and conditions for doing so may be particularly favorable now.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Un-American Capitalism
proj-syn.description: The current US administration's openly corrupt style of crony capitalism is the antithesis of the institutional foundation on which the US economy was built. The winners in the new oligarchic competition are not those who make the best products, but rather those who are best at flattering the mad king.

proj-syn.title: Can the Manchester Model Save Britain?
proj-syn.description: Following a decades-long effort to lay the foundations for economic dynamism, Greater Manchester has become the UK’s fastest-growing region. While the Manchester model cannot be precisely replicated at the national level, it does carry important lessons for outgoing Prime Minister Keir Starmer's likely successor.

proj-syn.title: How Trillionaires Are Really Made
proj-syn.description: Some may argue that the world’s first trillionaire is a story of technological triumph and a win for American capitalism. But markets have not bet on cutting-edge technology or a company too big to fail, but rather on the idea of a mega-monopolist with wealth and influence so vast that the US government will not allow him to fail.

proj-syn.title: Cities Show How Climate Action Makes Life Better
proj-syn.description: Cities have shown that a combination of adaptation measures and energy efficiency can save lives, improve well-being, reduce energy costs, and create conditions for sustainable growth. A new partnership seeks to help mayors and city leaders scale up these efforts through technical and financial assistance.

proj-syn.title: The Myth of Global Chaos
proj-syn.description: Today’s seemingly nonstop international tumult is not as unintelligible as it seems. What pundits lazily describe as chaos is the culmination of developments that were long in the making and arrived at a time when the international system was no longer able to prevent or mitigate geopolitical shocks.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.
